title: Effects of Addition and Multiplication of Constants

titles.subject: Statistics
titles.leaf: Effects of Addition and Multiplication of Constants

author: 696637e49d26457b33c7eff3
chapter_outcomes: Understand the effect on the mean and the standard deviation of adding a constant to each value and of multiplying each value by a constant.
Understand the effect on the median and the interquartile range of adding a constant to each value and of multiplying each value by a constant.

Understand the effect on a statistical measure of a distribution if extra values are introduced or some of the existing values are removed. For example, the median will increase, decrease or stay the same.

Calculate the mean and the standard deviation of a data set formed by combining two data sets with known means and standard deviations. Including use of the mean of one data set and the combined mean to find the mean of the second data set.

Use means and standard deviations of distributions to scale data values for comparison and interpretation. Including scaling to a given mean and standard deviation and standardising to a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1.

Make comparisons between distributions by considering measures of central tendency and measures of dispersion. For example, from known means and standard deviations of two distributions, identify the distribution with, generally, the larger values, and identify the distribution with, generally, values which are most consistent.
